model.name: Project Graze habitat classifier
model.selectionRule: Highest mean macro-F1 over the 4 leave-one-wilderness-area-out folds; a simpler model within 0.01 macro-F1 of the best wins (softmax < MLP < forest). Written before any LOAO result (docs/notes.md section 3).

classOrderNote: Class indices are a stable contract: the cover map, vegetation meshes and tints are keyed by index. Reordering or renaming a class requires telling Roles 1 and 2 first and bumping modelVersion.

dataset.name: Covertype (UCI Machine Learning Repository)
dataset.citation: Blackard, J. (1998). Covertype [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C50K5N
dataset.region: Four wilderness areas of the Roosevelt National Forest, northern Colorado, USA (30 m x 30 m cells)
preparation: Downloaded from UCI and verified by SHA-256 (ml:fetch).
Locked final test set: stratified 10% of all rows (58101), never used before the model freeze.
Model inputs built with @graze/features sampleToVector, the same function the app uses (aspect -> sin/cos).
Standardization (networks) and the OOD detector fit on training rows only; temperature and OOD threshold on a 15% inner holdout of the training rows.
Flexible models trained on a uniform subsample of at most 150000 training rows per fold.

split.description: Random splits put neighbouring, correlated 30 m cells on both sides, so they overstate accuracy. Holding out a whole wilderness area tests generalization to a new landscape, which is what the sandbox asks of the model.
details: Dev set: 522911 rows; locked test set: 58101 rows.
Random split of dev: 418329 train / 104582 validation (stratified).
LOAO fold, held-out Rawah: 288134 train / 234777 validation.
LOAO fold, held-out Neota: 496099 train / 26812 validation.
LOAO fold, held-out Comanche Peak: 294825 train / 228086 validation.
LOAO fold, held-out Cache la Poudre: 489675 train / 33236 validation.
Cottonwood/Willow occurs only in Cache la Poudre, so it is unseen in training when that area is held out.

calibration.method: Temperature scaling fitted on the inner holdout and folded into the last layer; bins are on the random-split validation

ablations.name: terrain
ablations.description: The deployed contract: FEATURE_NAMES from @graze/features (9 values). LOAO mean macro-F1 shown; random split 0.486.

ablations.name: terrain-no-hillshade
ablations.description: Contract features without the three hillshade columns. LOAO mean macro-F1 shown; random split 0.451.

ablations.name: terrain-no-water
ablations.description: Contract features without horizontal/vertical distance to water. LOAO mean macro-F1 shown; random split 0.434.

ablations.name: all-original
ablations.description: Contract features plus the excluded original columns: distance to roads and fire points, 4 wilderness-area and 40 soil-type indicators. Evaluation only; generated terrain has none of these. LOAO mean macro-F1 shown; random split 0.581.

featureImportance.method: Permutation importance: mean drop in macro-F1 when one feature is shuffled (3 repeats, up to 20000 validation rows per fold); mean over the 4 LOAO folds

ood.description: Root-mean-square z-score of the 9 model features against the training mean/std. Threshold = 99th percentile of distances on in-distribution holdout rows, so about 1% of normal rows are flagged by design. It measures distance from the centre of the data, not unusual combinations of normal values.

generatedTerrain.generator: packages/sim/terrain generateTerrain (Role 1), inputs from @graze/features heightmapToInputs, predicted by the app engine; water cells excluded
generatedTerrain.flagDefinition: flaggedRate = cells the app marks low trust (OOD detector over threshold OR any input outside its training range). detectorFlaggedRate and outsideTrainingRangeRate split it and sum to flaggedRate.

worlds.name: sandbox-page-defaults
worlds.description: Sandbox page on load: relief 0.2, band center 0.4, 12% water, roughness 0.5, valley 0.35

worlds.name: generator-defaults
worlds.description: generateTerrain defaults: relief 0.2, center 0.5, 12% water, roughness 0.5, valley 0.35

finalModelHoldout.note: Inner holdout of the dev set (also used for temperature and OOD threshold); not the locked test set.

limitations: Predicts the mapped cover type of 30 m cells in four Colorado wilderness areas from terrain alone; it knows nothing about soil, climate, fire history or disturbance.
Soil type, wilderness area and distances to roads and fire points are excluded because generated terrain has none of them; the all-original-features ablation shows what that costs.
Spruce/Fir and Lodgepole Pine are most of the data; accuracy mostly reflects those two classes, so macro-F1 and per-class recall are reported.
Leave-one-area-out results vary a lot between areas; a held-out area can contain classes or elevations the training areas barely have.
Generated terrain is synthetic; hillshade and water distances are computed differently from the GIS layers behind the dataset.
The OOD flag is a distance from the training centre; it cannot catch inputs that look typical feature-by-feature but never occur together in real landscapes.

Walk-mode vegetation and overlays draw the predicted class of each cell of generated terrain. The terrain is not a real place, a good-looking world is not evidence that the model is accurate, and low-trust (OOD) cells are drawn differently because their predictions are guesses.
Educational simulation only, not a forest-management or ecological decision tool.
